initial_plan.can_answer: partly: it can compare recorded crash frequency per clock hour at night versus daytime, but cannot establish per-trip or per-mile danger because traffic exposure is absent
initial_plan.metric: number of police-reported crashes per observed clock hour
initial_plan.denominator: the count of calendar dates in the included years multiplied by clock hours in the period (14 daytime hours: 06:00–19:59; 10 nighttime hours: 20:00–05:59); unknown-time crashes are not assigned to either period
initial_plan.population: one row per police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crash, in complete calendar years available in the file, with a usable crash_date; group by crash_time into daytime, nighttime, or unknown
filters: exclude rows with missing or unusable crash_date from yearly/date denominator
retain crashes with missing/unusable crash_time as unknown time, not day or night
initial_plan.years: all complete calendar years represented in the file, to be identified by the data check
initial_plan.grouping: daytime (06:00–19:59), nighttime (20:00–05:59), and unknown crash time

data_check.facts: See check_1.csv. The file covers 2012-07-01 through 2026-06-11; complete calendar years are 2013–2025. Among dated crashes in those years, there are no missing dates or times; because crash_date and crash_time are typed DATE and TIME columns, no empty, unknown-string, or impossible date/time values are represented. There are 23,787 midnight timestamps. There are 2,132,218 dated crashes in those years before the time-quality filter; 2,108,431 have non-midnight times and are the final population. The partial years 2012 and 2026 have 100,545 and 36,424 dated crashes, respectively.
data_check.meaning_and_decisions: Exclude the partial years so they do not contribute fewer days to the comparison. Exclude the 23,787 midnight records from day/night classification because midnight is piled up at a potential default and assigning it to nighttime could distort that group; no crash_date or crash_time values are missing in the dated full-year candidate data. Change the grouping from an unknown-time group to day and night only, with the uncertain midnight records disclosed as excluded. Compare recorded crash frequency per clock-hour slot, using calendar days × 14 daytime hours or × 10 nighttime hours as the denominator.

final_plan.can_answer: partly: compares reported crash frequency per clock-hour slot by time period, but not risk per trip, person, vehicle-mile, or traffic exposure
final_plan.metric: average number of police-reported crashes per clock-hour slot per calendar day
final_plan.denominator: sum of calendar days in 2013–2025 multiplied by 14 daytime clock-hour slots (06:00–19:59) or 10 nighttime clock-hour slots (20:00–05:59)
final_plan.population: one row per police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crash dated in full calendar years 2013–2025, with crash_time not equal to 00:00; 2,108,431 crashes
filters: exclude midnight timestamps (00:00) as potentially default/uncertain time
no missing dates or times among the dated full-year candidate records
final_plan.limitations: Crash reports do not provide traffic exposure, so this describes recorded crashes per clock-hour slot rather than risk per trip or mile. The 23,787 midnight-timestamp crashes are excluded as potentially default time values; the partial years 2012 (100,545 dated crashes) and 2026 (36,424) are excluded.
